[[Category:Killycurragh Townland, Derryloran Parish, County Tyrone]]
== Biography ==
This account represents the record-defined father associated with Killycurragh, Derryloran, County Tyrone. Held marriage accounts name David as father of Jane in 1850, James in 1855 and John in 1865. More than one local David may be represented: the named roles do not by themselves prove all adult identities or establish this David’s own parents. His father remains unknown.

The separate FamilySearch G3NQ-1FY claim of a David who died in Indiana on 13 March 1866 is an unproved identity lead and is not adopted as this man’s death or migration. Existing estimated date fields remain provisional.

<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/119f603202309 Irish civil marriage, Jane Glasgow and James Ferguson, Cookstown1850; held cited account reused].</ref><ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/e663a73250139 Irish civil marriage, James Glasgow and Hanah Ferguson, Cookstown1855; held cited account reused].</ref><ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/7de79d3055078 Irish civil marriage, John Glasgow and Jane Bell, Cookstown1865; held cited account reused].</ref><ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/18970220/048/0003 Funeral of Mr James Glasgow, Killycurragh, Mid-Ulster Mail20 February1897 p3; held cited account reused].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
This profile is for people whose father is "David Glasgow, Killycurragh" and born around the 1830s. It's possible there might be more than one such person.

No records found for this David in the Civil Registration suggesting he died before 1864.  There is a David Glasgow in Griffith's, but not clear which as there were younger David Glasgows as well.

Birth set as "before 1803" based on 21 years before youngest known child.

Links between children:
* Son [[Glasgow-1711|James]]'s funeral is attended by brothers John and David.
* [[Glasgow-1727|Jane (Glasgow) Ferguson]]'s brother James Glasgow is "brother-in-law" at the funeral of [[Glasgow-1653|Nancy (Glasgow) Henry]] . However, David's son [[Glasgow-1711|James]] 's wife is Hannah, the sister of James Ferguson.  So this actually does not prove that Jane and Nancy are sisters.
* [[Darragh-255|William John Darragh (1899-aft.1945)]] is "cousin" of [[Ferguson-16811|Mary Jane Ferguson (1895-1911)]]; this is not possible but they would be second cousins if [[Glasgow-1706|John]] is indeed the son of this David.
* The funeral of granddaughter [[Ferguson-16693|Martha Ferguson (abt.1870-1898)]] cites "David Glasgow, uncle" (i.e. David is a son of this David).

For extra research notes see:
* [[Space:Glasgow_of_Killycurragh%2C_early_C19]]

An ancestry tree cites [[Henry-6408|Mary (Henry) Glasgow (abt.1803-1888)]] as his wife. However the death registration calls her "married" whereas she should be a widow, so this seems less likely.
